title: The One-Boot Puzzle
learning_objectives: Use matching marks as a clue, then check a guess by watching how prints are made.
Compare whom Grandma and Sam each plan a stepping game for.

rights.media_license: family-use, original SVG by GitHub Copilot (AI)

parent_prompts: Before reading: What might make a row of boot prints without anyone walking in those boots?
After page 4: Why does Sam think a nick might explain the matching gaps in the big prints?
After reading: How does Sam turn the answer to the puzzle into something for Mo?

pages.text: Sam found footprints in Grandma's smooth sand patch. Each mark showed the bottom of a big boot.
pages.image_alt: Sam crouches low, leaning over to inspect a row of boot prints in smooth sand while Mo watches.
pages.image_provenance: Original SVG by GitHub Copilot (AI), 2026-10-21; independently reviewed
pages.audio_script: Sam found footprints in Grandma's smooth sand patch. Each mark showed the bottom of a big boot.

vocabulary.definition: Marks left where feet or boots press down.
vocabulary.example: The footprints show where a boot touched the sand.

pages.text: A trail of marks curved around an empty flowerpot. Sam wondered why the prints made two circles.
pages.image_alt: Two rings of boot prints surround an empty flowerpot as Sam and Mo look down at them.
pages.image_provenance: Original SVG by GitHub Copilot (AI), 2026-10-21; independently reviewed
pages.audio_script: A trail of marks curved around an empty flowerpot. Sam wondered why the prints made two circles.

vocabulary.definition: A line of marks that you can follow.
vocabulary.example: The trail bends around the flowerpot.

pages.text: Sam made two prints beside the trail. His left and right boots made different shapes in the sand.
pages.image_alt: Sam steps beside the large boot prints, leaving a left and right pair of smaller prints.
pages.image_provenance: Original SVG by GitHub Copilot (AI), 2026-10-21; independently reviewed
pages.audio_script: Sam made two prints beside the trail. His left and right boots made different shapes in the sand.

pages.text: Each big print had the same little gap. Sam wondered if a nick in a boot had made it.
pages.image_alt: Sam points to matching notches on two large boot prints in the sand.
pages.image_provenance: Original SVG by GitHub Copilot (AI), 2026-10-21; independently reviewed
pages.audio_script: Each big print had the same little gap. Sam wondered if a nick in a boot had made it.

vocabulary.definition: A small cut in an edge.
vocabulary.example: The nick leaves a gap in the boot print.

pages.text: Sam guessed that one boot had made the big prints. He asked Grandma how one boot could walk alone.
pages.image_alt: Sam gestures toward the boot prints while Grandma listens beside the sand patch.

pages.audio_script: Sam guessed that one boot had made the big prints. He asked Grandma how one boot could walk alone.

pages.text: Grandma lifted an empty boot from behind the flowerpot. She pressed it into the sand with both hands.
pages.image_alt: Grandma grips a purple boot with both hands, pressing its notched sole onto the sand in a fresh print beside the flowerpot.

pages.text: Grandma had made a stepping game for Sam. The two circles gave him a longer path to follow.

quiz.prompt: Why did Sam ask how one boot could walk?

options.text: To check his guess about the prints
To ask Grandma to teach him hopping
To ask for boots in his size

quiz.explanation: Page 4 gives the matching gaps in the big prints as a clue. Page 5 says Sam guessed one boot made the big prints and asked Grandma how, suggesting he wanted to check his guess.

quiz.prompt: What do Grandma's trail and Sam's trail show about their plans?

options.text: Each makes a game for Grandma
Each makes a game for someone else
Each makes a game for both at once

quiz.explanation: Page 7 says Grandma made a stepping game for Sam. Page 8 says Mo wanted a turn and Sam made a tiny trail with a toy boot, so each planned a game for someone else.

quiz.prompt: What made Sam decide to stamp another trail?

options.text: Grandma wanted him to start again
Sam wanted to practise making circles

quiz.explanation: Page 7 says the first stepping game was for Sam. Page 8 says Mo wanted a turn after Sam finished, which explains why Sam made the next trail for him.

quiz.prompt: Tell how Sam's one-boot guess turned out to be right, and what the trail was for.
quiz.rubric: not yet: names a boot or a print without explaining the puzzle; with support: links the matching gaps to a possible boot nick or names the stepping game after a prompt; independent: connects the matching big prints as a clue with seeing Grandma stamp one empty boot and explains that two circles make a longer stepping game for Sam
quiz.explanation: Pages 4 and 5 give Sam's clue and guess; pages 6 and 7 reveal Grandma's method and the purpose of her trail.

activities.prompt: Put these events in story order.

items.text: Sam finds big boot prints in the sand.
Sam tries making prints with his own boots.
Grandma presses an empty boot into the sand.
Sam stamps a tiny trail for Mo with a toy boot.

prompts: Which would help you test the one-boot guess: the shape of each print or the number of circles, and why?
How could Sam change his little trail to give Mo a longer stepping game?

off_screen_prompt: Trace a spoon to make a trail for someone else. Explain how your plan is like Grandma's and Sam's.
